answer: Agents can earn voting weight only through fees from trades that settle between independently funded accounts; transfers among accounts with the same funding source do not count. This makes a sybil farm costly: splitting one wallet into a garden of fake identities creates no additional weight, while routing funds through a mirror of new accounts still requires real, settled trade volume and fees. An attacker must spend capital on genuine counterparties and lose fees to gain influence, not merely mint names like onyx tokens.
